title: Rework kernel probing and version stitching for heterogenous GPU environments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce production incidents and weird degradation cases caused by mismatched kernel symbols and quantized binary variants across NVIDIA driver/CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combinations. Deliver a deterministic runtime probing and version-stitching layer that picks the smallest safe kernel variant, ensures ABI compatibility checks, and provides graceful fallback profiles when optimized kernels are unavailable. This is a refactor and compatibility hardening task (not new public API).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime detects CUDA driver/driver toolkit combination and resolves a compatible kernel candidate within 150ms on cold start
When optimized CUTLASS kernel is incompatible, runtime falls back to alternate kernel profile without request failure and with <10% request error rate increase in canary traffic
End-to-end canary on a dedicated GPU pool for CUDA 11.8, 12.2, and 13.0 with Triton v2/v3 shows no increase in P99 latency beyond SLA thresholds
All new probing logic covered by unit and integration tests that run in CI matrix (CUDA 11/12/13 x Triton 2/3 x sm_70/80/90)
Rollout plan documented and rollback capability implemented (flag + automatic fallback to previous probing resolver)
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after on-call incident where a small fraction of requests hit a CUTLASS symbol mismatch on CUDA 12 nodes; postmortem recommends deterministic probing and smaller fallback profiles.

2025-02-12 - Marco Liu: Spike completed. Implemented prototype resolver that probes exported symbols and checks symbol version table. Prototype found three mismatches across our internal perf pool when testing with driver 535.54; will extend heuristics to include kernel metadata tags.

2025-02-17 - Marco Liu: Design discussion notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Kernel+Probing+Design. Decided on two-layer approach: (1) cheap runtime probe for fast decisions, (2) optional binary-level verifier in slower path for canaries and CI. Trade-off: slight binary size increase vs reliability.
2025-02-20 - Sarah Gomez (review): Suggested adding a signed manifest per kernel build to avoid accidental cross-deployment regressions; created follow-up ticket PM-512 for CI signing flow.

2025-02-24 - Marco Liu: Branch pushed - github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427. Changes: probing API, host-side kernel registry, and a new fallback profile table. Unit tests added for symbol lookup shim. Benchmarks attached to PR comment.

2025-02-26 - Eng QA (Elliot Park): Integration test run across CUDA 11.8/12.2/13.0 on sm_80 uncovered a 200ms cold-start regression when the verifier path is enabled. Investigation shows verifier does synchronous ELF parsing which blocks startup; added async verifier and micro-batching of verification tasks.

2025-02-28 - Marco Liu: Canary rollout scheduled for 2025-03-03 on 5% of dedicated pool (non-prod first). Canary plan: 24h traffic ramp, monitor P50/P95/P99 latencies, error rate, and 'kernel_fallback' metric. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/gpu/compatibility?panel=kernel-probing

2025-03-01 - Performance: Initial microbenchmarks show end-to-end throughput improves by 6% when successful optimized kernel selected; fallback path has 8-12% higher token costs depending on sequence length. We will add cost-accounting labels for visibility.

2025-03-02 - Security: Verified fallback table cannot be overridden by tenant config; manifest signing discussion required for runtime-1.23. Marking security_review_required=false for this patch, but recommend follow-up for signing (PM-512).

2025-03-02 - Marco Liu: Roadmap next steps: finish async verifier, add signed manifests in CI, add more matrix entries (Triton 3.1), and wire automatic rollback based on 'kernel_fallback_rate' threshold > 3% per hour. Updated due_date to 2025-03-15 to account for test matrix expansion.
